title: Community Dining Room
blurb: Four questions about Singapore's hawker centres.
fact: Hawker centres are Singapore's community dining rooms: strangers share tables regardless of religion or diet.
credit: Facts from the National Heritage Board's Roots entry on hawker culture. Text and art are original.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many hawker centres are there in Singapore?
questions.note: Over 110, most of them in the neighbourhood centres of public housing estates.

options: Flat bread with stretched dough and ghee
questions.note: Stretched dough and ghee. The soup noodle is laksa and the salad is rojak.
Stir-fried flat noodles. Skewered meat is satay.

questions.prompt: Who built Singapore's first hawker centres?
options: Hawkers and communities, with government help
questions.note: In the early years of independence, hawkers and communities worked with the government, giving hawkers steady livelihoods and everyone affordable meals.
